theory.target: Certify one rational degree-three polynomial-Gaussian Cohn-Elkies candidate in dimension 24 and compare its exact bound with a degree-one calibration.
definitions: u=pi*|x|^2, n=24, m=12; Fourier convention uses exp(2*pi*i*<x,y>).
f=P(u)*exp(-u), hat(f)=Q(u)*exp(-u); signs are quantified over all real u in their half-lines.
Candidate family Q=(u-b)^2*(u+c); exact finite grid specified in input.json.
Density is covered volume fraction; it differs from center density by unit-ball volume.
assumptions: Cited Cohn-Elkies packing theorem and standard Gaussian Fourier identity; no kernel acceptance.
Polynomial-Gaussians are Schwartz; transforms may be differentiated under the integral.
Global signs come from factor/Taylor identities, not finite samples.
Canonical source is a heading; no reconstruction, novelty or autonomous parent-problem claim.
approaches_considered: Mesh, derivative margin and infinite-tail certification after square-factor removal; considered but not implemented.
Exact positive factorization for Q and nonpositive shifted coefficients for P, paired with rational Fourier coefficients.
falsification_targets: Wrong Fourier convention, transform coefficients or center-density scaling.
Negative between-grid values, double-root instability, undersized tail threshold and zero denominator.

claims.statement: In dimension 24, P(u)=225+13u+13u^2-u^3 and Q(u)=(u-15)^2*(u+1) are Fourier-paired polynomial-Gaussians with positive equal origins and correct global signs at T=15; the cited Cohn-Elkies theorem gives density at most 21357421875/1322849927168.
claims.falsification_condition: The transform identity, any global sign, positivity, admissibility or density normalization fails, or the cited theorem is inapplicable.

claims.statement: Among the 70,200 configured grid triples passing the specified sufficient certificate test, b=15,c=1,T=15 minimizes the exact bound; 13,135 pass. This bound is strictly smaller than the degree-one baseline, without any broader optimality claim.
claims.falsification_condition: An accepted grid triple has a smaller bound, counts or digests disagree, or the exact baseline comparison fails.

claims.statement: Positive values on the quarter-grid suffice to certify nonnegativity between grid points. This shortcut is false for the stored cubic negative-dip control.
claims.falsification_condition: A polynomial is positive at every tested quarter-grid point but negative at a point between them.

claims.statement: The 2017 primary authors abstract establishes a prior Leech-lattice optimality result in dimension 24; the present weak calibration is not a new optimal packing claim. The AIM heading itself was not freshly verified.
claims.falsification_condition: The cited abstract does not support that historical prior-result boundary or the packet incorrectly claims fresh AIM verification.

progress.summary: Produced a finite exact certificate with P(15+v)=-30-272v-32v^2-v^3 and Q=(u-15)^2*(u+1), independently reproducible density objective, and a strict improvement over the degree-one baseline.

checks.method: Start with seven certificate mutations and a between-grid counterexample; derive Fourier coefficients via the radial Laplacian, tail coefficients via exact derivatives, then replay the finite grid and check the objective.
checks.independence_basis: Fresh python -I process reads input.json and untrusted certificate.json only. It imports no theory code or output. Radial differentiation and factor multiplication replace the theory Laguerre/binomial transform. Same assistant authored both; no independent human/model review.
checks.result: All mutations rejected; 121 positive samples miss a -1/1000 dip. The full 70,200-triple replay agrees on 13,135 accepted triples, ordered digest and winning bound. All 36 transform-involution basis checks pass.
blocking_objections: The cited packing theorem and analytic Fourier identities are not kernel checked or independently human/model reviewed.
Finite-grid optimality does not imply optimality among arbitrary auxiliary functions.

checks.method: Read original Cohn-Elkies Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 and the 2017 primary authors abstract; audit equal origins, radius scaling, volume factor and prior-result boundary.
checks.independence_basis: Primary PDF and primary abstract retrieved separately from imported dataset summaries; distinct verification notes. Same-assistant review, not a fresh-model referee.
checks.result: The equal-origin theorem fits the displayed candidate after the global sign audit; converting center density gives the exact rational objective. Prior optimality result is explicit; AIM source itself was unavailable.
blocking_objections: AIM source heading and imported general certificate lemma remain unverified; human scope review required.

progress.summary: An independent algebraic implementation regenerates the certificate and entire finite search, rejects seven bad certificates, and stores an exact counterexample to sampling-only positivity.

unresolved_objections: Canonical source is a broad heading and the AIM page could not be retrieved; human scope review remains necessary.
Only a weak dimension-24 calibration and finite-grid search are certified; no state-of-the-art or general imported-lemma claim.
Published packing theorem and analytic steps are cited/derived but not kernel accepted or independently human/model reviewed.

next_step: Retain this exact Fourier/sign/objective certificate as a regression baseline; human-review the source heading before higher-degree or broader-dimensional work, and rotate to the next eligible ranked candidate.
